ce_bugs.text: packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73 — A collective cohost uses the first host's calendar ID with their own credentials, so Office365 creation fails or targets the wrong calendar instead of their destination (also affects Lark and CalDAV).

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:449 — Cancelling all occurrences of a collective booking repeatedly deletes only the first reference with organizer credentials, leaving cohosts' newly created events active after the series is marked cancelled.
packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:171 — Changing destinationCalendar from an object/null to an array silently breaks webhook and integration consumers that parse the existing payload shape.
packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — Google Meet bookings without a destination calendar dereference undefined and fail instead of falling back to Cal Video.
packages/core/EventManager.ts:370 — Passing every host the full destination array makes Office365, Lark and CalDAV target the first host's calendar and fail to create other hosts' events.
packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — When the organizer has no destination calendar, optional push discards all collected cohost calendars and their events are never created.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:257 — Legacy references without externalCalendarId now resolve no calendar for updates instead of using the destination calendar, breaking rescheduling.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:148 — Destinations without credentialId no longer match any Google credential and silently create bookings on primary instead of the selected calendar.
packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:449 — Cancelling all remaining collective occurrences repeatedly deletes only organizer references and leaves cohost calendar events active.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:449 — The recurring-series deletion batch runs once per calendar reference, multiplying remote deletes by the reference count and causing severe latency and provider rate-limit pressure.
packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — Empty destination-calendar arrays make Google Meet booking creation throw before fallback processing.

mrv_findings.text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — P1 confidence 100: `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")` dereferences undefined when Google Meet is requested without a destination calendar, throwing instead of executing the existing Cal Video fallback.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:170 — P1 confidence 100: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined,` discards every video meeting's credential ID, so handleCancelBooking's credential-gated deleteMeeting branch skips cancellation and leaves the external meeting alive.

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73 — P1 confidence 100: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` always chooses the first host's calendar while EventManager invokes this adapter with each host's credential and the complete destination array, making additional Office365 hosts write to another account's calendar or fail instead of receiving events; Lark and BaseCalendarService retain the same first-element routing defect.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — P1 confidence 100: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);` silently discards all collected cohost calendars when the organizer and event type have no destination and initialize the field to null, so these collective hosts never receive their calendar events.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:147 — P1 confidence 100: `const selectedCalendar = calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId;` cannot match legacy destination rows with a null credentialId even though EventManager explicitly supports them, silently moving their bookings from the selected calendar into primary.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — P1 confidence 100: `: event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` searches for the missing externalCalendarId rather than falling back to a configured destination, causing updates of references without calendar IDs to send an undefined calendarId and deletions to target primary instead of the previously supported selected calendar.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:454 — P1 confidence 100: `const bookingRef = updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"));` still selects only one reference using only the organizer's credentials inside each newly added host iteration, so cancelling all remaining occurrences repeatedly deletes the first host's events while leaving other collective hosts' events scheduled.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:208 — P2 confidence 100: `externalCalendarId: result.externalId,` now consumes metadata that CalendarManager.updateEvent never returns and the adjacent credential assignment loses the former destination fallback too, so updateLocation emits calendar references without the calendar/credential routing identifiers needed for later operations.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151 — P1 confidence 100: `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}),` reverses the previous slug condition, so billing-disabled organization creation now persists neither slug nor requestedSlug and loses the requested organization address.

packages/features/ee/payments/api/webhook.ts:229 — P1 confidence 100: `destinationCalendar: selectedDestinationCalendar ? [selectedDestinationCalendar] : [],` reconstructs only the organizer destination before `eventManager.create(evt)`, leaving paid collective bookings without the additional hosts’ destination-calendar events (the PayPal and confirmation paths likewise omit the additional destinations).

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:454 — P1 confidence 100: `const bookingRef = updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"));` handles only the first reference using the organizer’s credentials in the all-remaining-occurrences branch, so cancellation of a collective recurring series leaves other hosts’ calendar events behind despite the new outer multi-reference loop.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:554 — P1 confidence 100: `const oldCalendarEvent = booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"));` leaves the booking-merge lifecycle restricted to deleting one old calendar event after updating all destination references, leaving stale events on additional hosts’ calendars when a multi-host booking is merged.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151 — P1 confidence 100: `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}),` reverses the existing organization-slug billing condition, omitting slugs when billing is disabled and assigning them immediately when enabled, an unrelated organization-provisioning behavior change outside the collective-host destination-calendar fix.

apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts:249 — P1 confidence 100: the only modified test asserts `destinationCalendar: [],` for a rejected booking, so it never exercises two hosts with distinct destination calendars or checks their create/reschedule/cancel side effects, allowing the central multi-host routing change to regress while this test passes.
